ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Information for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT Act, Act No. 1, 2021), the Commercial Act (Act No. 1, 2021), and the Financial Transactions Reports Act. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) and the Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) mandate UBO identification for corporate accounts and transactions. The Act on the Protection of Personal Information also governs.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in Korea: If issued by a Hague Apostille Convention member state, obtain an Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state. If issued by a non-member state, obtain consular legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that state. The document must be notarized prior to apostille/legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same as above: Apostille for member states, consular legalization for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the resolution, then obtain an Apostille (if parent company is in a member state) or consular legalization (if non-member).
Notarize and then apostille or consular legalize as appropriate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the shareholder or parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize and then apostille or consular legalize as appropriate.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, beneficial owners, and senior persons against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own list (Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Additionally, conduct enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the Korean AML/CTF Act. This includes verifying source of funds, obtaining senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. All screening must be documented and retained for at least five years. The screening process must be automated and include fuzzy matching for name variations and transliterations. Positive hits must be escalated to the compliance officer and reported to the KoFIU as required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (Internet Registration Service)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean (Hangul) for registration, but may include English or other foreign characters if transliterated. The name must be distinct from existing registered names. For foreign entities, an English name may be used, but a Korean transliteration must be provided. The four-tier naming convention includes: (1) the corporate name (e.g., 'Chusik Hoesa'), (2) the business purpose, (3) the location of the head office, and (4) the company's specific name. The name must not contain prohibited words.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Supreme Court Registry Office within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written explanation of why the name should be accepted, along with any supporting evidence. The Registry Office will review the appeal and issue a decision within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Administrative Court. Alternatively, the applicant may modify the name and resubmit a new application. The reservation period is 30 days, and an extension of up to 30 additional days may be granted upon request and payment of a fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Contract Research Organization (CRO) engaged in clinical trial management, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not permissible. The Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and the National Tax Service require a physical office where trial data, personnel, and records can be inspected. Banks also require a physical office for account opening and AML compliance. The company must have a registered office in Korea with a physical address, including a meeting area, secure storage for documents, and a designated compliance officer. Virtual offices may be accepted for administrative purposes but not for core business operations. The tax authority may reject a virtual office for VAT and corporate tax purposes. Therefore, a physical office lease is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Verify that the registered office is a physical location with a signboard; (2) Ensure that the office is staffed during business hours; (3) Maintain all corporate records and trial data on-site; (4) Have a designated person responsible for regulatory compliance; (5) Ensure that the office is accessible for unannounced inspections. Risk of unannounced physical inspection: High (80%) for CROs due to regulatory oversight by MFDS and the National Tax Service. Inspections may occur quarterly or upon any red flag. The company must be prepared for immediate inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended by Act No. 20407), Part III Company Law governing the Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa), in particular Articles 288 (promoters), 289 (contents of Articles of Incorporation), 295 (subscription in full at incorporation), 302 (methods of subscription), 306 (receiving institution for subscription money), 317 (registration of incorporation), 352 and 356 (share certificates and register), 373 (board resolutions), 400 (director indemnity), and 409 (auditor appointment); supplemented by the Notary Act for certifying the Articles of Incorporation and by the applicable commercial registry regulations of the Supreme Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court, Judiciary of the Republic of Korea (Supreme Court registry system KECREG; electronic filing portal for commercial registrations); post-registration business registration administered by the district tax office under the National Tax Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Commercial Registration of Incorporation filed under Article 317 of the Commercial Act (registered capital, directors, auditor, seal, and registered office).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None statutory minimum: since the 2014 amendment to the Commercial Act, a Chusik Hoesa may be incorporated with any stated capital amount. The full subscribed amount must nonetheless be deposited into a dedicated temporary subscription account (escrowed with a licensed bank under Article 306) and remains blocked until the District Court Registry issues the certificate of incorporation registration; a working capital base of at least KRW 100 million is recommended to demonstrate operational solvency to multinational sponsors, insurance counterparties, and the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety in clinical trial sponsorship contexts.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA

DATE: ________; VENUE: REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY.

PRESENT: All founding subscribers constituting the inaugural board of directors of the Company, duly appointed in accordance with Part III of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, and the Articles of Incorporation.

WHEREAS:
(A) The Company has been incorporated as a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) for the purposes of clinical trial management, pharmaceutical research, and Contract Research Organization (CRO) services for multinational sponsors, subject to the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, the Korea Good Clinical Practice (KGCP) requirements, and the supervision of the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety;
(B) The founding shareholders have subscribed for the entire issue of ordinary shares and have deposited the full subscription price into the temporary subscription account of a licensed commercial bank, in compliance with Articles 295 and 306 of the Commercial Act, pending the incorporation registration of the Company at the competent District Court Registry;
(C) The Company requires a binding corporate mandate covering share capital verification, banking relations, the registered office address, and the appointment of statutory officers, to take effect immediately upon registration.

NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS HEREBY RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE OF SHARES. The Board ratifies the full subscription of the shares of the Company and confirms that the entire issued and paid-up capital has been received and segregated in the subscription account. The Representative Director is instructed to issue ordinary share certificates to each subscriber and to maintain the register of shareholders pursuant to Articles 352 and 356 of the Commercial Act. The Board confirms that the paid-up capital is unconditionally available for lawful corporate purposes as of the date of registration.

2. RECEIPT OF SUBSCRIPTION MONEY. The Board confirms the designation of [BANK NAME] as the receiving institution of the subscription price and authorizes the release of the blocked funds immediately upon presentation of the certificate of incorporation registration issued by the Court Registry.

3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts the premises situated at [ADDRESS], within the registration jurisdiction of [DISTRICT] District Court, as the registered office of the Company, and authorizes execution of the lease agreement and the submission of the corresponding registration documents.

4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board designates [BANK NAME], [BRANCH NAME] branch, as the principal depository bank. The Representative Director, the Chief Financial Officer, and any two of the directors jointly, are hereby authorized to open current and foreign-currency accounts, sign banking mandates, issue operational instructions, and execute wire transfers subject to the two-signature rule for any individual payment exceeding USD 50,000 or an equivalent statutory threshold.

5. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints [NAME] as Representative Director (Dae-pyo I-sa, Chief Executive Officer), [NAME] as Standing Director and Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as Auditor under Article 409 of the Commercial Act. Each appointed officer accepts office, shall obtain a corporate seal certificate, and shall register the appointment with the Court Registry within the statutory period. The Board further appoints [NAME] as the responsible person for KGCP compliance and adverse-event safety reporting.

6. SEAL AND ANCILLARY MATTERS. The Board adopts the corporate seal, authorizes its affixation to the registration applications with the District Court Registry and the National Tax Service, and approves all customary ancillary expenses of incorporation.

7. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION AND INDEMNITY. All acts lawfully done by the officers in furtherance of this resolution before and after its adoption are ratified. The Company shall indemnify each director and officer in accordance with Article 400 of the Commercial Act with respect to liabilities incurred in good faith within the scope of this resolution.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall continue in full force until amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board of Directors.

Duly passed on the date first above written. SECRETARY SIGNATURE: ________ CHAIRMAN SIGNATURE: ________

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Founder Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office under the Korean Notary Act (e.g., Seoul Central District Notary Public Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders shall instruct a licensed notary public to authenticate the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the corporate purpose clause referencing clinical trial management and CRO services, authorized and issued share capital, par value and classes of shares, board quorum and voting rules, statutory auditor appointment clause, and the registered office jurisdiction. Foreign subscribers must produce certified passport copies and, where applicable, a notarized power of attorney as well as a Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) report authorization granted to Korean counsel. The notary will verify the identities of all founders and confirm that the purpose clause does not violate mandatory provisions of the Commercial Act, pharmaceutical regulations, or public policy before certifying the document.
required_dossiers: Bilingual draft Articles of Incorporation
Certified copies of subscriber passports
Notarized power of attorney for each foreign subscriber
Legal opinion confirming FIPA eligibility and business scope
Application form for notarial certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification, Korean counsel shall obtain the written statement of refusal with the specific legal grounds, promptly revise the purpose clause or capital provisions accordingly, and resubmit the corrected Articles for notarization within one business day; any unresolved statutory objection will be escalated to a senior attorney review before the registration step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Temporary Subscription Account and Deposit of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed under the Banking Act of Korea (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Corporate formation counsel opens a dedicated temporary subscription account (subscription payment purpose account) in the name of the company being incorporated, submitting the notarized Articles of Incorporation and executing standard anti-money-laundering and Know Your Customer declarations under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information. Each founding subscriber then transfers the full subscription price into this account, and the receiving bank issues the certificate of receipt of subscription money on the closing date of the payment period. The deposited funds remain escrowed and blocked until the District Court Registry issues the certificate of incorporation registration, in accordance with Articles 302 and 306 of the Commercial Act; the bank mandate must name the Company as the sole beneficiary and prohibit premature withdrawals.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber identity and beneficial ownership declarations
Bank AML/KYC questionnaire
Subscription payment order forms
Certificate of incorporation name reservation
Bank certificate of receipt of subscription money
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a KYC query or requests supplemental beneficial ownership documentation, counsel shall promptly file the required declarations and source-of-funds statements with the same bank; if the bank remains unsatisfied, counsel shall terminate the instruction, select another licensed commercial bank, and re-run the deposit procedure within the same business day without forfeiting the notarized Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court, Judiciary of the Republic of Korea (KECREG electronic registration portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Korean counsel files the incorporation registration application under Article 317 of the Commercial Act through the Supreme Court registry system, attaching the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank certificate of receipt of subscription money, the minutes of the first board resolution, the written consents to office executed by the Representative Director and Auditor, the corporate seal specimen, and the notarized power of attorney authorizing the filing agent. Registration tax and education surcharge are paid electronically. The Registry verifies compliance with mandatory capital, officer and address rules and, upon satisfaction, issues the certificate of corporate registration and the corporate seal certificate; the Company is legally formed as of the date of this registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Commercial Registration of Incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of receipt of subscription money
Minutes of the first board resolution
Consent to office by each director and auditor
Corporate seal specimen and certificate
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Registration tax and education surcharge receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a correction order, counsel shall complete the required amendments within the statutory supplementary period, generally two weeks, by filing the requested supplemental documents such as corrected address proof or revised officer consents; failure to cure within the period results in automatic refusal, in which case the entire application is resubmitted within three business days with the deficiencies cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office under the National Tax Service (HomeTax online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days after the court registration of incorporation, counsel files the business registration application with the competent district tax office to obtain the business registration certificate, designating the ISIC 7490 service code and the corporate tax classification under the Corporate Income Tax Act. The tax office verifies that the Company maintains a fixed place of business at the registered office, holds a valid lease or ownership document, and is operated by an authorized representative director. After issuance, the Company may issue electronic tax invoices under the Value-Added Tax Act, open its official payroll and social-insurance accounts, and begin contractual billing to clinical trial sponsors; the business registration number becomes the Company's permanent tax identifier.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease or ownership certificate
Identification document of the representative director
Application for business registration
Confirmation of e-tax invoice issuance eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the physical existence of the registered office, counsel shall submit supplemental evidence comprising photographs, floor plans, and the lease certificate, or relocate the registered office to a compliant physical address, update the Registry registration accordingly, and resubmit the business registration application without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: MFDS Clinical Trial Plan Authorization and KGCP Compliance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Clinical Trial Management Division, through the MFDS electronic submission portal and the national clinical trial information system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each multinational drug trial, the CRO as sponsor-designated organization files a clinical trial plan application under Article 34 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, covering the protocol, investigator's brochure, informed consent form, investigator curriculum vitae and GCP training certificates, institutional review board opinion, and proof of clinical trial insurance or sponsor indemnity. The CRO simultaneously declares compliance with Korea Good Clinical Practice (KGCP) issued by MFDS notice, including standard operating procedures for trial master file custody, electronic data integrity aligned with 21 CFR Part 11 principles, investigator site monitoring, serious adverse event reporting, and audit trail maintenance. After MFDS validates the application, clinical trial activities may commence only from the date of approval or the running of the statutory no-response period, and all subsequent protocol amendments must be filed through the same portal.
required_dossiers: MFDS clinical trial plan application form
Clinical trial protocol and all amendments
Investigator's brochure
Informed consent form template
Institutional review board (IRB) approval opinion
Investigator CVs and GCP training certificates
CRO-sponsor contract and liability insurance evidence
KGCP compliance statement and SOPs
Serious adverse event and safety reporting SOPs
Electronic data integrity validation report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS requests supplemental scientific-technical data or issues a suspension, counsel and the CRO safety officer must respond within the period specified in the deficiency notice with the requested dossier; if MFDS refuses approval, the sponsor or CRO may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Health and Welfare within 90 days under the Administrative Appeals Act while continuing permissible preparatory site and documentation work pending the appeal outcome.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Clinical Trial Management Division; industrial and physical licensing per se not applicable to the office-based CRO service model under ISIC 7490.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Clinical Trial Plan Authorization under Article 34 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act; ongoing CRO operational scope governed by Korea Good Clinical Practice (KGCP) notice of the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, with electronic system validation and audit trail requirements for multinational trial data.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, delegated implementation to the Korea Environment Corporation (KECO) for registration-class environmental categories.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. ISIC 7490 clinical trial CRO management is a professional consulting and managed service with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing process at the registered office; therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment, prior environmental review, or environmental registration is required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act for the current scope. Conditional note: if the CRO subsequently adds a bioanalytical laboratory or an investigational product depot classified under ISIC 3xxx or 52xx, the operator must complete an environmental registration for the relevant small-scale air-pollutant-emitting facility or wastewater-discharge facility before commencing operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable for the office-based CRO scope. Conditional quantitative benchmarks if a future laboratory or depot is added: effluent discharge standards under the Water Environment Conservation Act of BOD 40 mg/L, COD 40 mg/L, and TSS 40 mg/L for industrial wastewater; volatile organic compound (VOC) fugitive emissions reporting triggered at the 10 tonnes-per-year facility threshold under the Clean Air Conservation Act; hazardous waste including expired investigational products, chemical reagents, and clinical trial residue must be transported and treated through the Allbaro manifest system with a licensed hazardous waste contractor.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Approval: Certificate of Completion of Fire-Fighting Facilities issued by the local fire safety authority under the National Fire Agency for the registered office premises, verifying egress routes, fire extinguishers, evacuation signage, and emergency lighting before occupation. Occupational Safety and Health: mandatory enrollment in the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance with the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service, and submission of the basic occupational safety and health management report under the Occupational Safety and Health Act; structural load inspection and electrical facility inspection of the leased premises as applicable for office occupancy, with additional requirements only upon any future laboratory or cold-chain storage expansion.

stage_2.regulatory_note: This Stage 2 dossier addresses statutory incorporation, corporate governance, and industrial/physical licensing for a Chusik Hoesa operating as a Contract Research Organization under ISIC 7490; clinical trial activities remain subject to MFDS protocol-level approval for each trial under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act and Korea Good Clinical Practice.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; administrative portal Home Tax Service (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Korean Chusik Hoesa with a domestic place of business must complete court registration of incorporation, obtain its corporate registration number, and then file a business registration application with the competent district tax office within 20 days of business commencement. The NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number that serves simultaneously as the corporate TIN and VAT registration number. For a foreign corporation without a local place of business that nevertheless has a Korean VAT nexus, registration is effected by filing the non-resident business operator registration form with the competent district tax office, either directly or through a Korean tax representative, accompanied by notarized foreign corporate certificates, the foreign registry extract, articles of incorporation, board resolution authorizing the Korean registration, power of attorney, and evidence of a Korean bank account for refund purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Korea does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa; it is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax and VAT. A qualifying domestic parent-subsidiary group may elect consolidated corporate taxation when direct or indirect shareholding satisfies the statutory threshold, allowing the group to file a single tax return and offset inter-entity profits and losses. Hybrid mismatch rules derived from the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs and BEPS Action 2 must be observed; any contractual election that recharacterizes payments, instruments, or entities for foreign tax purposes is disregarded for Korean tax classification unless explicitly recognized by statute.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The Korean VAT Act imposes no general turnover threshold for registration; any business supplying taxable goods or services in Korea, including a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa, must register before or at the time of business commencement. A simplified taxpayer concession exists for qualifying small-scale individual businesses whose annual taxable supplies are below KRW 80 million, but this does not remove the VAT registration obligation and is not available to a Chusik Hoesa. Non-resident electronic service suppliers who are required to account for Korean VAT are subject to the separate NTS foreign business operator registration regime with a de minimis annual turnover floor of KRW 1 million for Korean-source electronic services; a foreign entity with a Korean domestic place of business is outside that de minimis and must register a domestic business TIN.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All ordinary VAT taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices through the Home Tax System certified e-invoicing infrastructure. The e-invoice data is transmitted to NTS in near real time through APIs and national clearance channels; the NTS validates the invoice against taxpayer registration status, supply dates, and VAT return declarations. Failure to issue or transmit an e-invoice by the statutory deadline triggers a nondeductible additional VAT of 2% of the supply value. Korean law does not require a government stamp on each invoice, but the continuous fiscal validation and reconciliation function operates as a mandatory electronic clearance and audit trail.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Korean CRO Chusik Hoesa may apply the 0% export VAT rate for clinical trial management services supplied to a non-resident pharmaceutical sponsor or contract principal where the services are rendered to a non-resident, contracted in foreign currency, and paid from abroad. Services supplied wholly to non-residents and foreign-exchange-earning services constitute zero-rated supplies under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act. The CRO must maintain contemporaneous documentary proof of the non-resident identity of the customer, the actual performance and export nature of the service, the foreign currency invoicing, and the offshore receipt of consideration. Accompanying clinical trial materials physically exported from Korea are zero-rated as export goods upon completion of customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for physical cargo such as investigational drug samples and lab materials)
Bill of Lading or International Air Waybill evidencing outbound carriage from Korea
Clinical trial service agreement and detailed scope-of-work with the non-resident sponsor
Commercial invoice in foreign currency expressly showing 0% export VAT
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign exchange transaction confirmation showing payment from the non-resident counterparty
Certificate of non-resident status issued by the foreign sponsor's tax authority
Electronic tax invoice issuance record and Home Tax System transmission receipt
Internal cost allocation file demonstrating that the service value is not artificially shifted to export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is a high-risk audit area for NTS. The tax authority will challenge arrangements where export proceeds are not received within the statutory 180-day repatriation window, where foreign currency remittances are absent, where clinical materials are not physically exported under customs records, or where the foreign recipient lacks substantive existence. If the zero-rating is reversed, NTS imposes the unpaid 10% VAT plus a dishonest-tax-return additional tax of up to 40% of the understated tax, a 2% e-invoice related additional tax for missing or false electronic tax invoices, and late payment penalties. Frailulent claims expose the entity jointly and severally to retrospective clawback for up to five years, delisting of refund certificates, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including substantial fines and imprisonment of responsible officers and tax representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), exercising delegated foreign exchange administration jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and its Enforcement Decree; routine supervisory and reporting duties are further delegated to designated foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but not fully unregulated convertibility regime. Current-account receipts and payments are freely convertible without prior regulatory approval if routed through a designated foreign exchange bank and supported by underlying commercial documentation. Capital-account transactions are generally liberalized but are classified into three channels: fully liberalized transactions subject only to general permission, reportable transactions, and transactions requiring prior approval. For a Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in cross-border CRO services, the practical profit-remittance hurdle is tax and documentation rather than FX approval: dividends may be remitted only after a shareholders' meeting declares distributable profits, the company has satisfied mandatory statutory reserve requirements, Korean withholding taxes have been paid (generally 20% to 22% before applicable tax-treaty reduction), and the foreign-exchange bank has received the board resolution, audited financial statements, and tax clearance evidence. The FX bank then files the required foreign-exchange transaction report with the Bank of Korea; no separate prior BOK approval is required for an ordinary dividend remittance otherwise in compliance with FETA.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Korean FETA and the related Foreign Exchange Regulations impose a collection-and-surrender obligation on all exporters, including cross-border service providers such as a clinical trial CRO. The statutory rule requires that 100% of invoiced export proceeds be collected in South Korea through a designated foreign-exchange bank within one year from the export or settlement date, depending on the terms stated by the bank. There is no mandatory percentage that must be converted into Korean won because Korea has formally abolished forced foreign-currency surrender; the exporter may lawfully retain collected proceeds in a resident foreign-currency account. However, the proceeds must be credited to the CRO's Korean bank account and the corresponding foreign-exchange transaction report must be filed by the bank. For a CRO, each inbound sponsor payment must be supported by a master services agreement, milestone certificate, tax invoice, and the bank's foreign-exchange declaration to satisfy the export-proceeds verification rule.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Low for primary treasury purposes. Offshore digital electronic money institutions and cross-border fintech platforms are not licensed as designated foreign-exchange banks under the FETA and cannot independently open a Korean won settlement account for a Chusik Hoesa conducting clinical-trial services. Such platforms may be used only as an ancillary collection-engineering tool for small vendor payments or as an FX conversion intermediary outside Korea. The mandatory local regulatory rail is a licensed Korean commercial bank able to file foreign-exchange transaction reports, issue tax support documentation, and provide commercial clearing connectivity. Legal constraints under the FETA and Electronic Financial Transactions Act prevent an unlicensed offshore EMI from acting as the CRO's primary treasury clearing location.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A fully remote corporate account opening without any human verification is not permitted for a newly formed Korean CRO under Korean financial regulator guidance. A representative who is either a resident Korean director or an authorized local signatory must generally attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank branch. A non-resident foreign director does not always have to appear physically if the bank accepts a notarized and apostilled power of attorney appointing a local resident signatory, together with an authenticated board resolution, the director's passport copy, and a live video conference with the bank's compliance officer. In all cases the bank will require the original corporate registration certificate, certified Chusik Hoesa articles of incorporation, shareholder register, and evidence of the authority of any attorney-in-fact.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity caused by a Cayman, BVI, or similar offshore SPV holding the Korean Chusik Hoesa with unidentified natural-person shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation of the offshore parent entity; register of directors and register of members; full ownership-chain chart identifying every natural person holding 10% or more; statutory declaration tracing the ultimate beneficial owner; source-of-wealth documentation for each principal owner; completed bank KYC and beneficial-ownership questionnaire; industry-compliant sanctions-screening result for the full ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign non-resident directors acting only through power of attorney, which creates identity-verification and authorization-risk concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled or notarized board resolution approving the account mandate; original power-of-attorney form naming the Korean resident signatory; certified true copy of each director's passport; no-change certificate from the home corporate registry; live-video identity-verification recording if permitted by the bank; current corporate registry excerpt from the Korean court registry showing the registered officers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Clinical trial scope involving human biological materials, patient data, and controlled medicinal products, which may trigger a pharmaceutical-license and bioethics review red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clinical trial authorization issued by the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety; Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval letters for every clinical site; signed master services agreement between the CRO and the overseas pharmaceutical sponsor; proof of Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance; informed-consent and data-transfer documentation; evidence of any required licensing of the Chusik Hoesa as a contract research organization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Named directors or sponsors whose identity matches, or approximates, persons subject to OFAC, UN, EU, or Korean FSS sanctions or represents a PEP-linked ownership structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions-screening printout for all shareholders, directors, and key counterparties; a precise explanation of any name-match result; a sanctions check on the underlying sponsor and its clinical-trial supply chain; evidence of compliance with Korean export-control rules for human samples or biological materials; legal-consultant opinion on cross-border trade-sanctions exposure where the red flag is material.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lumpy, high-value inward payments representing clinical-trial milestone fees that arrive before the underlying service period or without clear invoice-supporting detail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Milestone-based payment schedule extracted from the master services agreement; signed work-order or statement-of-work for each clinical trial; invoice and verified electronic tax invoice; CRO project progress report; sponsor acceptance certificates; intercompany treasury policy explaining the funding pattern; audited or management accounts of the Korean entity justifying the cash-flow need.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an inbound equity injection into the Korean Chusik Hoesa, the foreign investor must first ensure that the investment is reportable under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and FETA. The remitter wires funds by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own bank account to the designated foreign-exchange bank account of the Korean entity. The wire must clearly use the beneficiary CRO's official English name, its Korean business registration number, and a reference code matching the foreign-investment report number, with the purpose identifier clearly stated as FDI-CAPITAL-INCREASE. Before posting the funds, the Korean bank verifies the remitter name against the foreign-investment report, checks the source-of-funds evidence, validates the relevant Bank of Korea declaration, and only then credits the capital escrow account. The CRO must subsequently issue shares, file the foreign-investment closing report, and complete the Korean court corporate registry update. Loan-based injections must use the intercompany loan purpose indicator and must be supported by a notarized loan agreement, pricing evidence, and repayment schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments by a Korean CRO for international clinical trial services, investigator grants, laboratory fees, and biotech vendor charges are cleared primarily through bank wire transfers using the SWIFT MT103 system. Each disbursement must be supported by the underlying service agreement, a valid commercial invoice, an itemized milestone statement, and, where applicable, a withholding-tax certificate. The foreign-exchange bank will assign the appropriate Korean foreign-exchange transaction purpose code and automatically file the Bank of Korea declaration. Commercial letters of credit are not the standard clearing rail for intangible CRO services because the service delivery cannot be represented by bills of lading and presentation documents; LCs are used only for procurement of physical clinical-trial materials, medical devices, or pharmaceutical supplies where documentary presentation is commercially meaningful. The CRO should maintain segregated project accounts for sponsor-pass-through funds to preserve audit clarity and avoid co-mingling of reserves.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/KRW forward contract with a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank, provided the notional amount does not exceed documented CRO receivables or payables within the next 12 months.
FX swap transaction between the Korean CRO and an authorized domestic foreign-exchange bank to bridge mismatched milestone receipt dates and vendor settlement dates.
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) for long-term intercompany funding or sponsor loans, used solely to hedge currency and interest-rate mismatch rather than to create speculative profit.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) only where the bank confirms that the CRO is an eligible corporate participant and the hedge relates to a firmly committed clinical-trial currency exposure; in mainstream domestic treasury practice a deliverable forward is preferred for Korean residents.

Optional derivative structures, including zero-premium collars and participating forwards, offered by the bank's derivative dealing desk, provided the underlying transaction is evidenced and the hedge is maintained within the CRO's treasury-risk policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Adjustment Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by March 31, extendable to April 30 with an approved extension application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% to 20% of the underreported liability for failure to file or fraudulent underreporting, daily statutory interest on unpaid tax, asset seizure, tax delinquency publication, and potential registration cancellation and judicial dissolution for sustained non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting Financial Statement Approval and Minute Book Entry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Statutory Records; commercial registration court only for resulting changes in directors, auditors, or registered officers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held and financial statements approved within 3 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year companies must complete this by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act against representing directors for failure to convene the AGM; judicial correction orders and administrative penalties for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the electronic reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be issued within 90 days after fiscal year-end; audited financial statements must be submitted to the AGM within 3 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 100 million under the External Audit Act, FSS enforcement inspection, suspension or disqualification of appointed auditor, and risk of judicial strike-off for repeated statutory filing failures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent external audit when total assets at fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12 billion approximately USD 9 million, or when the company is listed, publicly traded, or holds certain regulated financial or pharmaceutical CRO licenses under the External Audit Act and related statutes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for public listed companies; Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) for private non-listed Chusik Hoesa entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose an annual beneficial owner re-confirmation filing. Transfers of shares are recognized by updating the shareholders' register, and the register must be maintained continuously at the registered office. Financial institutions and tax authorities may request UBO information during inspections or contractual review, but no calendar-year UBO confirmation is required by the corporate registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 to 1,200 per year for a registered office and registered agent service in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to 15,000 for a private CRO entity requiring a full statutory audit; USD 2,000 to 4,000 for review-level assurance when no mandatory audit applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive tax brackets for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2023: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; and 24% on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion. Preferential deductions and credits include the R&D tax credit for clinical trial process innovation (generally 25% for SMEs, up to 30% for new growth source technologies under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act), the job creation tax credit, the temporary investment tax credit, and foreign-investment incentives for high-value bioindustries.
